claim: A production Agent Skill encodes the SOP as a rigid 5-step MEASURE-IDENTIFY-FIX-VERIFY-GUARD workflow rather than open-ended instructions.
stance_target: Advanced Skill Sequences pillar — converting SOPs into deterministic Agent Skill sequences
scope_conditions: Real-world GitHub repo addyosmani/agent-skills, performance-optimization skill
quoted_support: 1. MEASURE -> Establish baseline with real data 2. IDENTIFY -> Find the actual bottleneck (not assumed) 3. FIX -> Address the specific bottleneck 4. VERIFY -> Measure again; keep or revert 5. GUARD -> Add monitoring or tests to prevent regression

claim: The skill defines explicit numeric acceptance thresholds for Core Web Vitals to gate whether an agent's optimization is accepted.
stance_target: Zero-Hallucination & Quality Control pillar — rigid evals with measurable pass/fail thresholds instead of subjective agent judgment
quoted_support: LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) Good <= 2.5s, Needs Improvement <= 4.0s, Poor > 4.0s; INP Good <= 200ms; CLS Good <= 0.1

claim: A change that shows no measurable improvement beyond run-to-run variance ('neutral') must be treated as a revert, not kept, to prevent unmeasured complexity from accreting.
stance_target: Zero-Hallucination & Quality Control pillar — rigid evals must reject neutral/unproven agent changes, not just negative ones
quoted_support: Within noise (no measurable change) -> Revert. ... "Neutral" is a revert, not a keep.
numbers: example: 3% gain inside +/-5% variance is not a gain

claim: The skill requires logging every optimization attempt including reverted ones in a short ledger (idea, baseline-to-result, verdict, why) to prevent agents from re-trying the same failed idea in future runs.
stance_target: Zero-Hallucination & Quality Control pillar — persistent memory of failed agent attempts reduces wasted compute/hallucinated re-attempts
scope_conditions: Performance optimization skill, applicable to any agentic SOP with iterative experiments
quoted_support: Reverted work leaves no trace in git history, which is exactly why the same dead idea gets tried again next quarter. Keep a short ledger so a discarded idea stays discarded.

claim: The skill enumerates explicit CI-enforceable performance budgets (bundle size, API p95 latency, Lighthouse score) that can be wired into automated gates for agent-authored code.
stance_target: Zero-Hallucination & Quality Control pillar — code blast radius containment via CI budget enforcement
quoted_support: JavaScript bundle: < 200KB gzipped (initial load) ... API response time: < 200ms (p95) ... Lighthouse Performance score: >= 90

claim: The skill explicitly rejects a 'win' that required breaking or skipping a test, labeling it a regression disguised as an improvement.
stance_target: Zero-Hallucination & Quality Control pillar — correctness must gate performance metrics to prevent agents gaming evals
scope_conditions: Verification step of the optimization workflow
quoted_support: Improved, but a test went red -> Revert. A regression wearing a win's clothing.
